reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: Draft judged: “It should make sense to you and if it's something big or hard to undo, wait till you're calm and then check it out with what you know.” It replaces exactly the two sentences in SOURCE.txt (“It should make sense, too. Even then, anything big or hard to undo can wait until you're calm and you've checked it against what you actually know.”), appears once in CONTEXT.txt (the end of the paragraph after “Once you get an answer, you can ask…”), and sits directly after his unchanged “If it tells you to do something, I'd only do it if it's loving and leaves you free.” So it does what the_change says: one Emulate sentence for his two. MEANING: all four points survive: (1) it must make sense (the added “to you” only says to whom, which is the only sensible reading of a test on an inner answer, so it adds no claim); (2) anything big or hard to undo; (3) wait until calm; (4) check it against what you know. What moved: “can wait” becomes the imperative “wait” (permission to command; in a safety passage that is the safer direction and it changes nothing the reader is told to do); “Even then” becomes “and if” (the concession is carried by the extra rule following the two tests, and a big or irreversible instruction that failed a test would not be done anyway); “until you're calm and you've checked it” becomes “till you're calm and then check it” (same order, calm first and then the check, as the source lists them); “actually” is dropped (trivial). “check it out with what you know” is a loose collocation (nearer “check it out with someone” than “check it against”), but its sense is clear, it is casual speech, and I saw no Emulate artifact of the kind he has caught before: no space before a full stop, “it's” is correct, no stray quote marks. Typography nit, not a defect: the draft's straight apostrophes match the sentence right before it and the words it replaces, and the section already mixes straight and curly apostrophes (“doesn’t” in the last paragraph), so the draft adds no new mismatch. READ IN CONTEXT: I read the whole Core prompts section, then the sentence. A careful reader would not feel a seam: the run-on with no comma after “you” reads as talking, the second-person instruction matches how the section addresses the reader (“When you want to…”, “Once you get an answer, you can ask”), and the next paragraph (“that doesn’t make the answer automatically true”) still follows. The repeated “it” (the answer, then the thing it asks) has the same shifting referent as the source, so C02 is no worse. TELL ROWS: T01 ABSENT (no first person in the draft; his “I'd” is the unchanged line before). T02 ABSENT (one step in a three-sentence paragraph; no run of compressed commands). T03 ABSENT (follows from “If it tells you to do something”). T04, T05, T06, T07, T08, T10, T11, T12, T16, T17, T18, T19, T23, T24, T25, T27 ABSENT (no scene, prop, filler, image-plus-explanation, permission formula, bridge, matched pair, contrast, aphorism, announcement, scenery, faux-insight, colon reveal or tic word). T09 and T13 (the lint's D9 pointers) ABSENT: the draft is a single rule of thumb with its reason built in (“big or hard to undo”), uneven rather than equal-weight, and it adds and removes no aside or callback in a paragraph whose other sentences are his own. T14 ABSENT: nothing was reordered or moved; only a connective (“Even then”) and a modal were reshaped, and the point they carried is still there. T15 ABSENT on balance: the structure changed (two sentences to one) and the one off phrase is speech-like, not a thesaurus swap. T20 and T29 ABSENT: the closing line is a long plain instruction, not a polished closer or restatement; the paragraph has no new claim to cut. T21: closest row, and the linter's B4/E15 flag. It is two linked steps in one breath (a sense test; then wait, then check), the same jobs his two sentences carried and no new job, joined by a loose “and if” and “and then”, not a balanced list. I do not read it as a condensed function list. T22 ABSENT (a rule with its reason, not reassurance alone). T26 ABSENT. T28 ABSENT (not a section end). C01, C03, C04 ABSENT. LINT FINDINGS: B4/E15 accepted: see T21; the packing is the spoken join of his own two steps, with no items listed. D9 accepted: this is a sentence-for-sentence splice, so following the replaced passage's order is by construction; T13 and T09 checked above and neither is happening, because only one sentence changed and the rest is his. E36/E41 accepted: I counted the second person in the replaced words (“you're”, “you've”, “you actually know” = 3) and in the draft (“to you”, “you're”, “you know” = 3, which over its 28 words is the linter's 10.7 per 100), so the change adds none, and the section is addressed to “you” throughout. No unjustified tell, no added claim, meaning kept.
